We're looking for a Senior Research Associate who can find out anything about anything. Leadership will come to you with questions — size this market, map the players in this category, who's funding what, what the landscape looks like for XYZ — and you'll come back with an answer that's clear, well-sourced, and actually useful.

Some weeks that means building a competitive matrix across 40 companies. Some weeks it means a deep dive into a single obscure question nobody has written about yet. The projects change, the subject matter changes, and the volume varies week to week.

You'll be exposed to a lot of different projects and ideas, and work directly with a highly accomplished leader and team. If you're the kind of person who reads everything, asks a lot of questions, and wants to be in the room with people operating at a very high level, this is built for you.

What You'll Do

 - Run open-ended research projects using the internet as your primary tool: markets, products, companies, funding activity, competitive landscapes, people, technologies, regulation — whatever the question requires.

 - Turn messy findings into clean outputs: matrices, comparison tables, briefs, landscape maps, one-pagers.

 - Go deep enough to have a point of view, not just a link dump — flag what matters, what's uncertain, and what you'd look at next.

 - Use AI tools aggressively to move faster and go wider than a person could alone.

 - Build lightweight tools, scrapers, or trackers when a project calls for it.

 - Juggle several unrelated requests at once and reprioritize when things shift.

What We're Looking For

 - 2–5 years of experience and a bachelor's degree — you take a task and run with it, but you've got the reps to produce senior-level output: quick turnaround, sharp judgment calls, and less hand-holding needed along the way.

 - Brain power: sharp, curious, and able to reason through a question you've never seen before.

 - AI-native: You live in AI tools — Claude and Cowork, ChatGPT, Gemini, Hugging Face, whatever's newest. Ideally you can vibe code your way to a working script or prototype without waiting on an engineer. Bonus points if you've hit your usage limit more than once.

 - Comfortable in ambiguity: Vague briefs don't paralyze you. You take a first pass, come back with questions, and iterate.

 - Self-directed but coachable: You think independently, but you want to learn from people far ahead of you and take direction well.

 - Startup-minded: You're not looking for a corporate ladder. You want interesting problems, smart people, and range.

 - A strong writer: Your research is only as good as your ability to communicate it in a page or less.

Compensation & Benefits

 - Salary: The anticipated base salary range for this position is $100,000-$130,000. Actual compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, level, and location.

 - Benefits: Generous benefits package including medical, dental, and vision, 401(k) matching

 - Location: Can be remote in the US, with significant travel to Los Angeles

title: Financial Scriptwriter
description:
About Future Finance
 A capital-intelligence media brand - newsletter, LinkedIn, X and YouTube. Future Finance doesn't sell directly; it builds reach and credibility, then hands qualified demand to the rest of the group.
 The audience is US-based, 45-plus, net worth above $1M. They understand macro but don't know how to act on it - intelligent, busy, and sold to constantly.
 The brand register is calm, premium and institutional. It never slides into wealth-guru, outrage or doom media, because the audience we want won't trust that tone. This matters more than anything else in this hire.
 The role
 You write Future Finance's long-form YouTube scripts - 30 to 35 minutes, roughly 4,200 words, one per week - and own the research behind every claim in them, so every claim traces to a primary document. You also cut 3–4 short-form scripts from each episode for distribution.
 You do not pick topics and you do not own packaging (titles, thumbnails). That stays with the showrunner and the production agency. You do not name the channel's proprietary frameworks - those come from Salim. You may write about a mechanism he's already explained; you won't invent one and hand it to him to defend on camera.
 What success looks like
- One publish-ready script a week, minimum - four a month, delivered as a full package: research memo, six-beat hook, body, retention map, SHOW/SOURCE tags inline, self-scored review sheet.
- Clears the review gate at 7 of 9 or better on first submission, scored against the Future Finance Content Standard.
- Zero unsourced factual claims - every claim carries a SOURCE tag to a primary document, both sides of contested arguments get argued, and thin research gets flagged, never filled in with a plausible number.
- Retention targets on the finished episode - 70%+ first-minute retention, average view duration above the channel baseline.
- Compliance held on every script - no predictions, no recommendations, no certainty language about what happens next.
- Weekly execution - memo submitted ahead of packaging, attendance at the weekly review, Slack availability during working hours, deadline risk flagged the day it's known.
 Requirements 
 What we're looking for
- Sourcing discipline. You open the primary document, not the article about it, and can defend any claim in your own work on the spot.
- Finance literacy. You can read a 10-K, a central bank statement or a BIS paper and come out with an argument.
- Register control. You can raise a script's emotional voltage without reaching for wealth-guru or doom tools, and rewrite a hyped paragraph down without losing the stakes.
- Retention craft. You design open loops, pattern interrupts and a climax on purpose - and can draw the retention map because you built it that way.
- Writing for the ear. Scripted for a teleprompter: one idea per sentence, every term defined at first use, read aloud before submission.
- Comfort working inside someone else's frame. You flag a hole in the argument and stop - you don't hedge around it or quietly strengthen a claim the host can't defend.
- Proactivity, attention to detail, high standards, curiosity about macro and digital assets, and integrity about what you have and haven't checked.
 What you'll need to show us
 To reach an interview, you need to evidence all four of the following. We screen on evidence, not on our own read of the writing.
- Proven scale, in this category. Seven figures of cumulative views on finance, macro, investing or business long-form - or a verified 3x-plus outlier against a serious finance channel's trailing average. Must be 25-minute-plus long-form; short-form and 8-minute credits don't count. Retention data required (average view duration, first-minute retention - not view counts), shown live via YouTube Studio screenshare or confirmed by the channel owner. Screenshots alone, or channels you can't name, don't count.
- A high-value audience, not just a large one. What the channel sells, at what price, to whom - sponsor class and CPM are good proxies. Our viewer is 45-plus with $1M+ net worth.
- At least one sample in a calm, sourced, institutional register. If the whole portfolio is hype, get-rich or doom content, that's a disqualifier regardless of the numbers.
- Willingness to complete a paid work sample. One assigned title, five working days, $1,250 - paid whether or not we hire.
 How we'll hire
- Stage 1 - Past work review and interview. We read the actual work - not a summary or a list of links - against the four requirements above. If all four are evidenced, you move forward regardless of our personal taste in the writing.
- Stage 2 - Paid trial script. One assigned title, the Content Standard, five working days. Paid $1,250, whether or not you're hired - that's told upfront. You deliver: a research memo (two pages max, every claim sourced to a primary document, both sides of any contested argument argued); the hook (six beats, 70 words or fewer); the full script with SHOW cues and SOURCE tags inline; a retention map.
- Stage 3 - Contract → conversion. Trial script, then a contract which includes a 3 month trial period at the monthly rate, converting to a permanent seat on day 90 against the outcomes above.
 Benefits 
 What We Offer
- Competitive salary + performance-based incentives
- Company offsites
- Remote work
- High ownership, high-impact role

 The Research Analyst for the Advancing Universal Representation (UREP) Initiative works in a supporting research role to build and share evidence in support of the Initiative’s goal to advance policies and programs that support due process in the immigration system by: 1) expanding access to legal representation for immigrants facing deportation—with the ultimate goal to establish a federal right to government-funded counsel for all immigrants facing deportation who cannot afford an attorney—and 2) combatting the harms of immigration detention. The Research Analyst collects, manages, and analyzes primarily quantitative and occasionally qualitative data;  assists in the writing of reports and other research materials to support the Initiative’s strategic advocacy and policy priorities; fields rapid response research requests; conducts literature reviews; supports the generation and design of new research; reviews documents; and presents findings from research projects.      
 In this role, the Research Analyst reports directly to  the Principal Research Associate, with support and mentorship from the Research Associate, the Principal Data Scientist, and the Associate Director of Research for the UREP Initiative and will also develop and strengthen their own skills and work independently. The Research Analyst contributes to and supports discrete tasks but also has some task ownership and task management. The Research Analyst primarily works on qualitative research projects, which requires independent coding and analysis, and will also occasionally perform tasks beyond research-specific tasks, including some advocacy and administrative work.     
 The Research Analyst collaborates with team members to advance Initiative goals by actively engaging in team meetings and program activities. The Research Analyst is also expected to support efforts to ensure Vera’s Race, Equity, and Inclusion priorities are a core aspect of Vera’s mission, both internally in how team members work together, and in research, including in methodological approaches, publications, hiring and staffing, and external and internal research communications.

description:
Titan Wealth is a fast-growing wealth management business, both in the UK and internationally.  It has evolved a fairer, more efficient and effective business model, structured to deliver leading advice-led wealth management services, giving financial advisers and their clients the best opportunity to fulfil their dreams and ambitions.

We provide a dynamic work environment full of opportunity, one where both individual and team initiative and contribution is encouraged, so that together we can deliver better outcomes for our clients over the long term.


Due to continued growth through strategic acquisitions, Titan Wealth is expanding rapidly – offering a unique blend of entrepreneurial energy and the backing of private equity. It’s an exciting time to join the business.
Titan Wealth Planning (TWP) is a key part of the Group, focused on delivering best-in-class advice across wealth management, retirement planning and employee benefits.
We are now looking for a Financial Planner to join our Edinburgh office, inheriting and developing an existing client bank. This role offers a strong platform for an experienced adviser to focus on client relationships and high-quality advice delivery, with support from paraplanning and client services teams.
This role will see you inheriting a client bank of circa £50 Mil AUM with huge opportunity from an OTE perspective. 
This is a remote role, with some time spent in the Edinburgh office and meeting clients locally.


Responisbilities 
Client Management & Advice Delivery 
- Take ownership of an established client bank, providing ongoing holistic financial planning advice
- Deliver high-quality advice across pensions, investments, protection, tax planning and retirement strategies
- Maintain and strengthen long-term client relationships, identifying new advice opportunities
- Ensure excellent client outcomes, service standards and communication throughout the client journey
- Manage review cycles, ensuring clients receive proactive and timely engagement
- Generate additional revenue through client referrals and cross-selling opportunities
- Collaborate with wider Titan teams (investment management, employee benefits, etc.) to deliver integrated solutions
 Business Development 
- Identify and act on opportunities within your existing client bank
- Support organic growth through referrals and professional introducers
- Build and maintain relationships with external professional connections (accountants, solicitors, etc.)
- Contribute to local growth plans aligned with regional and national strategy
 Compliance & Governance 
- Provide advice in line with FCA regulations and Titan policies
- Maintain Competent Adviser Status (CAS) and ‘Fit & Proper’ requirements
- Ensure all client files and suitability reports meet compliance standards
- Stay up to date with industry developments and technical knowledge
- Operate in line with TCF principles at all times

About you 
Essential 
- Diploma in Financial Planning (or equivalent)
- CAS status / current SPS holder
- Proven experience managing client relationships as a Financial Planner
- Strong ability to deliver holistic financial advice
- Excellent communication and relationship management skills
 Desirable 
- Chartered Financial Planner status or working towards
- Experience managing or taking on an existing client bank
- Broad technical knowledge across all areas of financial planning
- Previous paraplanning experience

What We Offer
Immediate access to an existing client bank
Full paraplanning and administrative support
Clear pathway for continued career progression
Opportunity to work within a growing, acquisitive business
Exposure to a broad client base and more complex planning scenarios


Our employees are talented people, distinguished by excellence.  You will be able to demonstrate a willingness to embrace the Company values of:

Creativity – we recognise we need new ways of thinking, learning and doing to both improve our own productivity and efficiency as well as to help us stay ahead of competitors.

Commitment – we are team with the willingness to put time, effort and energy into driving change in the organisation, going the extra mile.

Collaboration – we need teamwork amongst ourselves and with partners to generate more innovative, efficient and effective solutions and thereby a greater sense of achievement.

ESN ist seit 2004 deutscher Marktführer für Sporternährung und bietet Produkte wie Proteinpulver, Riegel und Supplements, die auf ambitionierte Fitnessziele ausgerichtet sind. description:
About Anthropic 
 Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
 Anthropic Fellows Program overview 
 The Anthropic Fellows Program is designed to foster AI research and engineering talent. We provide funding and mentorship to promising technical talent - regardless of previous experience.
 Fellows will primarily use external infrastructure (e.g. open-source models, public APIs) to work on project aligned with our research priorities, with the goal of producing a public output (e.g. a paper submission). In one of our earlier cohorts, over 80% of fellows produced papers. We run multiple cohorts of Fellows each year and review applications on a rolling basis.
 Submit your application to the Economics & Policy workstream at the bottom of this page. We are accepting applications on a rolling basis for the next cohort expected to start in January 2027. In some circumstances, we can accommodate fellows starting outside the usual cohort timelines — please note in your application if the January 2027 start date doesn't work for you.
 What to expect 
- 4 months of full-time research 
- Direct mentorship from Anthropic researchers 
- Weekly stipend of 4,615 USD / 3,440 GBP / 6,470 CAD / 4,110 EUR + benefits (these vary by country)
- Substantial funding for compute and other research expenses
 Interview process 
 The interview process will include an initial application, assessments, and interviews. We may ask for references later in the process as well.
 We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.
 Compensation 
 The expected base stipend for this role is 4,615 USD / 3,440 GBP / 6,470 CAD / 4,110 EUR per week, with an expectation of 40 hours per week for 4 months (with possible extension).
 The Anthropic Institute Fellows (Economics & Policy) 
 Mentors, research areas, & past projects 
 Fellows will undergo a project selection & mentor matching process. Potential research areas and mentors include:
- Economics 
- Maxim Massenkoff
- Peter McCrory
- Policy, Security, and Society 
- Jack Clark
- Marina Favaro
- Jim Baker
 Projects in this workstream may include:
- Designing and conducting empirical research on AI's economic effects, drawing on external data sources
- Developing new methodological approaches for studying AI's impact on labor markets, the future of work, and society
- Analysing the offense–defense balance for AI-enabled cyber and bio capabilities as models scale
- Measuring the extent to which model performance increases with custom harnesses
- Identifying market driven mechanisms that could improve societal resilience to anticipated threats from AI systems
- Identifying which metrics relating to AI R&D could serve as early warning signals for recursive self-improvement
 For past project examples, see:
- How AI Impacts Skill Formation : Judy Shen and Alex Tamkin
- Stress-Testing Model Specs Reveals Character Differences among Language Models : Jifan Zhang, Henry Sleight, Andi Peng, John Schulman, and Esin Durmus
 Unique candidate criteria 
 You might be a particularly great fit for this workstream if you:
- Have an interest in economics or policy research; prior experience in this area is a plus but not required
 [...]  Logistics Requirements:  To participate in the Fellows program, you must have work authorization in the US, UK, or Canada and be located in that country during the program.
 Workspace Locations: We have designated shared workspaces in SF.  We are also open to remote fellows in the UK, US, or Canada . 
 Visa Sponsorship: We are not currently able to sponsor visas for fellows. To participate in the Fellows program, you need to have or independently obtain full-time work authorization in the UK, the US, or Canada.
 [...]  Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience
 Required field of study:  A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience
 Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position
 Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.
 Visa sponsorship:  We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.
 For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

title: Business Operations Lead
description:
About Us

Our mission: Eradicate health disparities by empowering the teams who care for underserved families.

BridgeHealthAI partners with Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) and community organizations to ensure every patient gets the care and benefits they deserve — without drowning care teams in paperwork. Our platform automates high-friction tasks like outreach, insurance verification, eligibility checks, follow-ups, and referrals. With modern AI and cloud infrastructure, we turn hours of manual effort into seconds, helping teams close care gaps faster, protect revenue streams, and stay focused on patients.

Born out of Harvard and MIT and backed by Pear VC, Flare Capital, and Glen Tullman (founder of Livongo), BridgeHealthAI is a fast-growing, seed-stage company trusted by leading community health centers. We are purpose-built for the safety net, helping clinics scale access, reduce burnout, and deliver equitable care for the 30M+ patients served by FQHCs each year.

The Role

We are seeking a full-time Business Operations Lead to own the day-to-day execution that keeps our platform running across 5+ health center clients. This is a high-ownership role at the center of how we deliver for clients — from data management and patient communication to client onboarding and QA.

You will work directly with our Head of Product and interact regularly with our engineering team. We are small, we move fast, and we are doing work that has a direct impact on patients. The right person is someone who is comfortable in the weeds, exercises real judgment, and genuinely cares about the communities our clients serve.

What You'll Do

Client and Patient Operations

 - Manage operational workflows across multiple health center clients, ensuring data accuracy and timely follow-through

 - Handle inbound patient responses to outreach campaigns — responding to general questions, providing guidance, and escalating appropriately

 - Support new client onboarding across use cases: coordinating approvals, managing communication templates, and ensuring a smooth go-live

Product Execution and Project Management

 - Own QA across outreach campaigns before they reach patients — reviewing content, flagging issues, and working directly with the engineering team to resolve them

 - Translate client feedback and QA findings into clear, actionable tickets for engineering

 - Support light product improvements — reviewing changes, providing feedback, and helping move smaller updates through to implementation

Supporting Marketing and GTM

 - Help create sales and marketing collateral — one-pagers, decks, and other materials to support outreach and client conversations

Required Qualifications

 - 3–5 years of experience in a healthcare, health tech, or healthcare operations environment

 - Hands-on experience with product QA or user acceptance testing — you have worked closely with a technical team to review and ship software

 - Experience supporting client onboarding or implementation at a software company — you know what it takes to get a client live

 - Strong written communication skills, especially for sensitive or patient-facing content — clear, warm, and accurate

 - Comfortable working with data — you can manage structured workflows, catch errors, and keep things organized across multiple workstreams

 - Detail-oriented — you catch things other people miss and care about getting it right before it reaches a patient

 - Self-directed — you can manage multiple priorities without needing someone to check in on you daily

 - Comfortable with ambiguity: we are early stage, processes are still being built, and priorities shift — you thrive in that environment, not in spite of it

Preferred Qualifications

 - Direct experience at an FQHC, Medicaid managed care plan, or health tech company serving safety-net populations

 - Familiarity with patient communication or outreach workflows in a healthcare setting

 - Exposure to early-stage startups or fast-moving product teams

What We Value

 - Mission-Driven: You care about equitable access

 - Operational Discipline: You work through complexity and complete tasks consistently

 - Detail-Oriented: You catch things before they reach a patient

 - Self-Directed: You manage priorities without needing daily oversight

 - Collaborative: You share insights that help us improve

 - Comfortable with Ambiguity: You build process where none exists

Why Join Us

 - Directly support patients accessing life-changing care

 - High-ownership role — you will shape how we deliver for clients at scale

 - Be an early team member building the operational foundation of a fast-growing company

 - Work at the intersection of healthcare, AI, and health equity

 - Competitive compensation at a seed-stage company backed by top investors

How to Apply

Please submit your resume and a brief note describing your experience in healthcare operations and what draws you to BridgeHealthAI's mission. We review applications on a rolling basis and will reach out to strong candidates for an introductory conversation.

Diversity and Inclusion

BridgeHealthAI is committed to building a diverse and inclusive environment. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds, including those with lived experience navigating the safety net. If you are passionate about the mission but do not meet every preferred qualification, we encourage you to apply.

 About Prolific 
 Prolific is not just another player in the AI space – we are building the biggest pool of quality human data in the world.
 Over 35,000 AI developers, researchers, and organizations use Prolific to gather data from paid study participants with a wide variety of experiences, knowledge, and skills.
 The role 
 We are seeking Director, VP, and C-Level Finance Professionals to join our expert B2B and AI research network. We provide high-level corporate intelligence for global organizations, and we require executive-level insights to validate complex financial data.
Please note: This is an invitation to join our expert talent pool. Participation in specific projects is not guaranteed and is subject to client demand and profile matching.

 Researchers looking for your skills tend to pay up to $100 You must be prepared to complete paid tasks that require one hour of uninterrupted work , though many are shorter.
 What you’ll bring 
- 
 Executive tenure: Proven track record at the Director level or above (CFO, VP, etc.).
- 
 Specialized knowledge: Deep expertise in corporate fiscal strategy, auditing, or financial modeling.
- 
 Professional profile: A verifiable LinkedIn presence or professional history. attention to detail and the ability to concentrate on complex tasks for up to one hour at a time
- 
 A reliable and fast internet connection and access to a computer
- 
 A willingness to self-declare your earnings, as our participants are self-employed
- 
 A Paypal account to receive payment from our clients
 What you’ll be doing in the role 
- 
 Strategic document audit: Review comprehensive financial reports (200–300 pages) to identify key fiscal drivers.
- 
 Executive consulting: Answer nuanced questions regarding corporate finance, risk, and strategy based on provided data.
- 
 B2B validation: Ensure research outputs reflect the practical realities of high-level financial management. willingness to take our skills verification test to assess your suitability for our participant pool
 Why Prolific is a great platform to join as a Participant 
 Joining our platform as a Prolific participant will give you the chance to influence the AI models of the future using professional legal expertise. Once you pass our assessment, you can join Prolific in just 15 minutes, and start enjoying competitive pay rates, flexible hours, and the ability to work from home.

 We believe that the next leap in AI capabilities won't come solely from scaling existing models, but from integrating diverse human perspectives and behaviours into AI development. By providing this crucial human data infrastructure, Prolific is positioning itself at the forefront of the next wave of AI innovation – one that reflects the breadth and the best of humanity.

title: AI Instructor – Specialization in Business & Finance Applications
description:
AI Instructor – Specialization in Business & Finance Applications 
 About Wall Street Prep 
 Founded in 2004 by investment bankers, Wall Street Prep (WSP) is a leading provider of professional skills training in financial and valuation modeling. Our mission is to bridge the gap between academia and the real world by equipping finance professionals and students with practical, hands-on skills.
 We partner with top-tier investment banks, private equity and investment management firms, Fortune 500 companies, and elite undergraduate and MBA programs. Our training is delivered through engaging in-person classroom sessions and via our industry-leading online learning platform, all designed by experienced finance professionals.
 Position Overview 
 Wall Street Prep is seeking an experienced and enthusiastic AI for Finance Instructor with a strong background in applying artificial intelligence, machine learning, and automation in business and finance settings. As an AI Instructor, you will join our elite team of instructors delivering cutting-edge training to professionals and students eager to master AI tools for real-world decision-making and business transformation.
 You will serve as a lead facilitator for immersive training seminars on foundational AI concepts, predictive analytics, generative AI, and the use of AI tools like LLMs, APIs, and Python-based automation—tailored to the business and finance context.
 This includes practical instruction on leading AI assistants and enterprise AI platforms such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, Perplexity, Rogo, and Shortcut, with a focus on how finance professionals can integrate these tools into research, analysis, and workflow automation.
 This is a unique opportunity to share your expertise, refine your teaching and public speaking skills, and help shape how the financial services industry leverages AI.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Deliver live in-person and virtual training seminars to corporate, undergraduate, and MBA clients, including:
- Financial institutions, consulting firms, technology teams, and corporate finance professionals.
- Top-tier MBA programs and executive education programs.
 Lead instruction in AI and machine learning concepts with a focus on:
- AI and generative AI fundamentals, including LLMs, embeddings, and transformers.
- Applied Python for finance, data analysis and visualization techniques, and automation workflows.
- Predictive analytics (regression, decision trees, random forests).
- Real-world use cases: fraud detection, churn prediction, stock return modeling, pricing optimization, and more.
- Demonstrating practical workflows using modern AI assistants and research tools such as ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Rogo, and Shortcut for tasks like investment research, financial analysis, workflow automation, presentation drafting, and knowledge synthesis.
 Collaborate on curriculum development, including:
- Updating and refining training content based on evolving AI applications in finance and business.
- Creating hands-on case studies that illustrate AI-driven business transformation.
- Contributing to elective modules in advanced AI integration, optimization, and automation.
- Designing hands-on exercises that teach participants how to use tools like ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Copilot for tasks such as financial analysis, data interpretation, coding assistance, research workflows, and productivity automation.
- Provide personalized mentorship through one-on-one tutoring sessions.
- Complete WSP’s Train-the-Trainer Program, a structured professional development initiative for new instructors.
 What We Are Looking For 
 Experience 
- 3+ years of experience in data science, machine learning, or AI implementation, preferably in finance, consulting, or a technology-forward corporate environment.
- Demonstrated experience building or applying AI solutions in business/financial contexts (e.g., forecasting, automation, investment research, fraud detection).
- Experience teaching or mentoring (corporate training, workshops, or academic instruction) is highly desirable.
- Hands-on experience using modern AI assistants and enterprise AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, Perplexity, Rogo, Shortcut) within professional workflows is strongly preferred.
 Education 
- Bachelor's degree in a technical or quantitative field required (e.g., Computer Science, Data Science, Finance, Engineering); Master’s or PhD a plus.
 Skills & Passion 
- Practical expertise using leading generative AI tools (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity) and AI workflow tools (Copilot, Rogo, Shortcut) for research, coding, productivity, and business analysis.
- Strong Python programming skills and experience with data science libraries (Pandas, scikit-learn, Matplotlib).
- Knowledge of AI frameworks (OpenAI API, Hugging Face, LangChain, etc.) and enterprise applications (Copilot, chatbots, etc.).
- Clear understanding of both technical and business-side AI use cases.
- A passion for teaching, mentoring, and empowering learners with real-world tools.
 Availability 
- Willingness to provide approximately 40 training days or more per year, including  enhanced availability during the summer months.
- Willingness to develop curriculum materials related to AI for use in both live and online training programs.
- The ability to conduct week-long or multi-week seminars is highly desirable.
- Flexibility to travel domestically and internationally.
 Compensation & Benefits 
 Compensation 
- Highly competitive daily rate.
 [...] - All travel and accommodation expenses covered by WSP.
- Paid professional development through WSP’s Train-the-Trainer Program.
- Opportunities to deepen your expertise in AI, analytics, and financial modeling.
- Expand your professional network across global finance and corporate sectors.
- Develop exceptional public speaking and facilitation skills.
 [...]

title: Senior Finance Consultant: Corporate Strategy & Research - Remote Advisory (Kraków)
description:
Senior Finance Consultant: Corporate Strategy & Research (Remote Advisory)
 About Prolific 
 Prolific is not just another player in the AI space – we are building the biggest pool of quality human data in the world.
 Over 35,000 AI developers, researchers, and organizations use Prolific to gather data from paid study participants with a wide variety of experiences, knowledge, and skills.
 The role 
 We are seeking Director, VP, and C-Level Finance Professionals to join our expert B2B and AI research network. We provide high-level corporate intelligence for global organizations, and we require executive-level insights to validate complex financial data.
Please note: This is an invitation to join our expert talent pool. Participation in specific projects is not guaranteed and is subject to client demand and profile matching.
 Please note, you will be asked to provide your LinkedIn profile URL when joining the waitlist so we can verify your experience.
 Researchers looking for your skills tend to pay up to $100 You must be prepared to complete paid tasks that require one hour of uninterrupted work , though many are shorter.
 What you’ll bring 
- 
 Executive tenure: Proven track record at the Director level or above (CFO, VP, etc.).
- 
 Specialized knowledge: Deep expertise in corporate fiscal strategy, auditing, or financial modeling.
- 
 Professional profile: A verifiable LinkedIn presence or professional history. attention to detail and the ability to concentrate on complex tasks for up to one hour at a time
- 
 A reliable and fast internet connection and access to a computer
- 
 A willingness to self-declare your earnings, as our participants are self-employed
- 
 A Paypal account to receive payment from our clients
 What you’ll be doing in the role 
- 
 Strategic document audit: Review comprehensive financial reports (200–300 pages) to identify key fiscal drivers.
- 
 Executive consulting: Answer nuanced questions regarding corporate finance, risk, and strategy based on provided data.
- 
 B2B validation: Ensure research outputs reflect the practical realities of high-level financial management. willingness to take our skills verification test to assess your suitability for our participant pool
 Why Prolific is a great platform to join as a Participant 
 Joining our platform as a Prolific participant will give you the chance to influence the AI models of the future using professional legal expertise. Once you pass our assessment, you can join Prolific in just 15 minutes, and start enjoying competitive pay rates, flexible hours, and the ability to work from home.
 We've built a unique platform that connects researchers and companies with a global pool of participants, enabling the collection of high-quality, ethically sourced human behavioural data and feedback. This data is the cornerstone of developing more accurate, nuanced, and aligned AI systems.
 We believe that the next leap in AI capabilities won't come solely from scaling existing models, but from integrating diverse human perspectives and behaviours into AI development. By providing this crucial human data infrastructure, Prolific is positioning itself at the forefront of the next wave of AI innovation – one that reflects the breadth and the best of humanity.

Prolific's  Candidate Privacy Notice  explains what personal information Prolific may process, where Prolific may process your personal information, its purposes for processing your personal information, and the rights you can exercise over Prolific use of your personal personal information.

title: Finance Officer
location: Home Based / with travel to the Edinburgh Office ; Remote
description:
The Finance Officer role works mainly within the Receivables part of the Finance team, supporting the integrity and efficiency of financial transaction processing and procedures related to a defined group of stakeholders (customers).  Supporting customers will involve ensuring the processing, delivery, recognition and payment of goods and services provided, processing grant support, donations from supporters and funding from partners.
 You will maintain the stewardship of resources within the organisation and service internal and external stakeholder needs by ensuring adherence to policy and procedures and managing the development of finance team processes and people.  You will support to the identification and management of risk within financial activities.
 The job on a day-to-day basis involves providing administrative and operational support for customer accounts, order processes and financial administration.  You will manage and process customer orders, invoices and account records, respond to and manage enquiries via email and phone, maintain accurate data and documentation, and work closely with colleagues and external partners to resolve queries and ensure efficient service delivery.  The role also supports wider business operations through reporting, payment administration, record management, audit support, and continuous improvement of processes, requiring strong organisational skills, attention to detail and confidence working with financial systems and databases.
 While the team is mainly home based, you will be involved in quarterly team-based face to face events and may support activities in the warehouse located in Edinburgh.  Ideally, you will be within a two-hour commute of Edinburgh.

We are looking for a collaborative, detail-focused professional who shares our commitment to DofE’s charitable purpose and social impact.  
 You will bring admin and accounting experience (AAT Level 4, ACCA/CIMA part-qualified or a relevant degree/HND or equivalent experience), alongside a strong understanding of accounting principles and hands-on experience of operating and financial transactions, reconciliations, and controls. 
 Curious and customer-focused, you’ll enjoy resolving problems, communicating clearly and collaborating with colleagues to deliver accurate, consistent services.  
You’ll be confident using Excel and Outlook, with the ability to make effective use of systems and contribute to their ongoing development.

If you feel excited by this role and believe you have the necessary skills and experience to become a valued team member, please go to our website and apply.
 The deadline for applying for this role is: Sunday 29th November -Midnight
 1st  interviews will take place on: Monday 14 December - Virtual via MS Teams
 The interview will involve a finance related written exercise 
2nd interviews will take place on: TBC if required. 
  If you would like to access the application form in a different format or if you would like any assistance that might help improve your experience while completing the application, please contact us by email  recruitment@dofe.org

Participate in a paid research study exploring how modern organizations manage financial and operational reconciliation infrastructure. Through a focused 45-minute remote interview, you will share insights into your organization's financial technology stack, internal processes, ownership structures, and operational priorities. -

 Describe your organization's reconciliation systems, financial technology stack, and existing infrastructure.

 Explain how finance and operations teams manage reconciliation workflows, responsibilities, and processes across departments.

 Share insights into internal ownership structures, accountability, and cross-functional coordination.
- 
 Discuss your experience evaluating, implementing, selecting, or managing reconciliation solutions and financial technology systems.
- 
 Explain how your organization identifies operational inefficiencies and prioritizes process improvements.
- 
 Share the strategic considerations, business objectives, and organizational needs that influence technology investments and infrastructure decisions.
- 
 Provide professional perspectives on current industry practices, operational challenges, technology adoption, and emerging priorities.
- 
 Discuss only genuine professional experiences and general organizational practices, without disclosing confidential or proprietary information.

 Currently employed in a senior leadership or management position within finance or operations.

 Direct experience managing, evaluating, overseeing, or significantly influencing financial and operational reconciliation infrastructure.

 Strong understanding of financial technology systems, reconciliation processes, and operational workflows.
- 
 Experience evaluating, implementing, or managing financial systems and technology solutions.

 Involvement in strategic technology investment decisions, financial transformation, or infrastructure planning.

 Ability to discuss organizational workflows, internal responsibilities, and professional experiences clearly during a remote interview.

CityHAP helps eligible households maintain stable, permanent housing by subsidizing their rent, with the household generally contributing 30% of its adjusted monthly income toward rent. The program provides targeted assistance to New Yorkers facing housing instability while helping preserve rent-stabilized housing and prevent homelessness.

title: Technical Business Analyst | Revyse
description:
How We Build 
 We don’t run sprints. Our company prioritizes the work together, and Engineers work in cross-functional pods. We leverage AI to draft most of our tickets, and Engineers write some of their own. There is no process layer standing between an idea and the code. That model moves fast, and it is only as good as the context feeding it. A confident, well-structured ticket that is wrong about how insurance requirements vary by trade can be painful. This role’s north star is to fix that. 
 You are not here to assign work or gate it, you're are here to make sure the right work is the easiest work to pick up. Your influence comes entirely from the quality of your context and the clarity of your case, which is either the best part of this job or the wrong job for you. 
 The domain has depth and complexity. Insurance requirements vary by trade, scope of work, and state. Compliance rules vary by customer. You will not be able to reason about our data without learning the domain, but don't worry - we'll give you time to learn it. 
 What you'll do 
 1. Context & Documentation 
- If AI drafts the tickets, the quality of what gets built is decided by the context it receives. That context is what you’ll optimize. 
- Understand and write down how the platform actually behaves today - the workflows, the exception paths, the rules, and the undocumented behavior currently living in people's heads. 
- Build and maintain the reference material that our AI tooling and our engineers pull from, and keep it accurate as the product changes. Stale documentation now produces bad tickets and bad code automatically, at scale. 
- Review tickets and specs against reality before anyone builds them. This is the part that matters most: AI-generated work is confidently wrong exactly where it costs the most - edge cases, compliance rules, customer-specific commitments, anything that is not in the repo or the training data. 
- Capture acceptance criteria, edge cases, failure behavior, and explicit non-goals so a pod can pick something up and build it without a meeting. 
 2. Product Data & Analysis 
- You’ll answer product questions with SQL against real data. Things like usage, throughput, drop-off, exception rates, workflow completion, turnaround times. 
- Quantify shipped work. Did it move the number it was supposed to move, and by how much. 
- Build and maintain the recurring reporting the pods rely on, so nobody rebuilds the same query every month. 
- Surface what nobody asked about. Note the distribution, the outliers, and the places where two numbers should reconcile and don't. The anomaly is usually the real finding. 
 3. Prototyping to Communicate 
- A working prototype settles an argument that a document might extend. You will build them constantly, and then engineers will rebuild the real thing. 
- Use AI tooling to build rough, working versions of an idea. A screen, a script, a query tool, a data view, so the team can react to something concrete. 
- Build small internal tools for yourself and the team where doing so is faster than asking for one. 
- Hand intent to engineers clearly. Your prototype is the argument, not the implementation. 
 Qualifications 
- 3+ years as a business analyst, technical analyst, product analyst, data analyst, or in product operations, working closely with engineers. 
- Strong SQL. You write your own queries against a real schema, you understand what a join is doing to your row count, and you sanity-check your results before presenting them. 
- You can read a database schema and work out how a product behaves from it. 
- You already work with AI as a daily tool, not an experiment. You know how to structure context so output is reliable, you iterate on prompts rather than accepting the first answer, and you know when a model is confidently wrong and you check. 
- You can build a rough working thing with AI assistance. Not production code. A prototype good enough that people can react to it instead of imagining it. 
- You write clearly. In a setup like ours, written clarity is not a soft skill. It is the input that determines what gets built. 
- Analytical honesty. You quantify rather than characterize, you name your assumptions, and when numbers don't reconcile you stop and investigate instead of shipping the chart. 
- Comfort operating without process scaffolding, and comfort saying “not this week, here's why” when three people want the same hour. 
- Bonus: B2B SaaS with enterprise customers, compliance- or workflow-heavy products, Python for analysis, or experience maintaining documentation that AI tooling depends on.

We're building finance at Pulley from zero to one, and this is the first hire. You'll own accounts receivable, accounts payable, and billing and invoicing, help run treasury, and build the processes, controls and automation those functions run on. You'll report directly to the VP of Finance.

This is a builder role, and at the start it is a hands-on one. You'll send the invoices, chase the payments, pay the bills, release the wires and talk to customers yourself. Then you'll make each of those faster, more accurate and less manual. We're looking for someone who isn't afraid to roll up their sleeves and who loves building the platform finance grows from. You're scrappy and love applying AI.

Our customers are national retailers, developers, and construction teams, which means vendor portals, milestone billing, lump-sum payments, and AP departments with their own processes.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Customer Setup & Contracts: Review billing terms on new contracts, complete supplier registration, and record each customer's billing requirements: legal entity, PO rules, portal and payment terms.

 - Collections: Own the aging report and run a set collections cadence. Work with sales, permit managers and customer AP teams to clear past-due invoices, and report aging and days sales outstanding weekly.

 - Cash Application & Disputes: Apply payments, including lump sums that cover many invoices, and resolve short-pays, disputes, credits and missing POs. Be the first point of contact for customer billing questions.

 - Accounts Payable: Run payables end to end: vendor onboarding, bill intake and approval, payment runs, corporate cards and expenses.

 - Treasury: Help manage cash day to day: send wires and payments, monitor balances, and maintain a 13-week cash forecast.

 - Payroll & Equity: Run payroll with our provider, and keep the cap table current: option grants, exercises and support for 409A valuations.

 - Processes & Controls: Write the playbook for each function, set approval limits, fix the upstream causes of errors, and support the month-end close our accounting team owns.

 - Systems & Data: Own the finance stack (Stripe, QuickBooks Online, HubSpot), keep data flowing cleanly between systems, and make sure the numbers can be trusted.

 - You're a builder. The third time you do something by hand, you write it down or automate it.

 - You have high agency. You see a problem and solve it without being told where to look.

 - You have high integrity. You can be trusted with the company's cash and its data.

 - You write clearly and warmly to customers and vendors, and you follow through until an issue is closed.

 - You use AI every day and love working with it. You've applied it to improve processes and workflows, and you're not afraid to do that here.


NEED TO HAVE

 - Experience with milestone or project-based billing, or a construction-adjacent background.

 - Hands-on experience with workflow automation tools.

description:
JOB PURPOSE: 
 This position is responsible for CenterLight’s billing and revenue cycle analysis, reconciliation, and operational procedures while maintaining adherence to DOH and CMS guidelines. This position independently manages day-to-day revenue cycle operations, reporting on revenue cycle functions, and provides guidance to Revenue Cycle Analyst I staff.
 JOB RESPONSIBILITIES: 
- Perform weekly billing for Best Choice/Matter of Care in coordination with Coordinators and Payroll.
- Enter and independently reconcile insurance and member payments to A/R.
- Perform full analytics on all revenue operations for all Line of Business of Centerlight.
- Perform analytics (on MMR and 820/834) and reconciliation of payments received to billing files.
- Independently investigate and resolve Enrollment/Intake discrepancies for correction/rebilling.
- Coordinate with Enrollment on PDE rejections and assist the Enrollment team with CMS-related issues.
- Coordinate with Enrollment on MSP letters and correction of discrepancies in ECRS.
- Identify members with Surplus, NAMI, or Pool Trust balances and resolve related issues.
- Work with the Enrollment/Intake team to resolve eligibility issues.
- Perform monthly MMR analysis and work with the CMS MAPD Helpdesk to open and resolve tickets.
- Coordinate with Dialysis providers to obtain 2728 forms and work with the CMS MAPD Helpdesk to activate member ESRD indicators.
- Prepare monthly GL entries related to revenue.
- Assist Actuarial with data analytics as needed.
- Develop and maintain financial reporting and analytics in Tableau/Power BI (including KPI dashboards) used by senior leadership to track actual results vs. target.
- Prepare ad hoc financial modeling, analysis, and projections.
- Serve as a resource and informal mentor to Revenue Cycle Analyst I staff on daily tasks, tools, and procedures.
- Contribute to process improvement initiatives and document standard operating procedures (SOPs).
- Create SQL queries/ store procedures for use by other members of the team.
- Work of developing process to identify revenue enhancing opportunities.
- Work on special projects as assigned.

- Proficiency in data analytics, i.e. SAS, SQL is required.
- Claims adjudication and understanding of claims PPS is strongly preferred.
- Knowledge of Medicaid and Medicare benefits, enrollment and billing, and provider contracting is required.
- Knowledge of CPTs, ICD 9/ICD 10, HCPC, DRG, Revenue, RBRVS.

- Ability to work independently while managing multiple studies and priorities.
- Ability and willingness to travel nationally approximately 80%, including air travel and overnight stays.

 Success in this position requires much more than taking meeting notes and converting them into requirements. The successful candidate must be comfortable challenging assumptions, identifying missing requirements, modeling complex processes and system interactions, analyzing data needs, and continuing discovery until the development team has a clear and testable definition of what must be built.

Our Sales team needs a dedicated data partner, and creator commerce https://kit.com/features/commerce (how creators monetize by selling digital products) is becoming a bigger part of how Kit and our creators scale. Kit is growing, so we're looking for a Senior Analytics Engineer to own Kit's sales and commerce data from end to end.

Accurate sales data gives our team a clear picture of the pipeline and the confidence to make informed decisions. That’s what makes this role so important.

Your primary focus will be Sales: the dbt models that turn our CRM data into trusted pipeline, deal, and funnel metrics, and the Omni dashboards our sales leader and Senior Revenue Operations Manager use to run the business. You'll also model creator commerce data, so we understand what creators sell and earn through Kit, and you'll pick up reporting work with our Product team, such as feature usage reporting. On a small data team, we step outside our usual lanes when the need is there, so the mix will shift over time.

You'll build for two kinds of consumers: people and AI. Teammates increasingly answer their own questions by querying our semantic layer through Omni's AI and MCP connections to AI tools. That means your models, metric definitions, and documentation need to be clear and correct enough for an AI agent to use them without a data teammate in the loop.

Share a written reflection with the team on what you've learned and where you'd focus first.

Sourcing and outreach

 - You will write and run outbound campaigns over LinkedIn and email, and you will own the quality of that writing rather than sending templates someone else wrote.

Screening

 - You will conduct first round conversations with candidates across both the Strategist and Forward Deployed Engineer tracks, which requires you to understand what strong performance looks like in each.

 - You will assess candidates against our rubrics for technical depth, client presence, and ownership, and you will help improve those rubrics as you learn where they produce the wrong answer.

 - You will make screening recommendations and explain your reasoning to hiring managers, including in the cases where they initially disagree with your read.



Hiring data

 - You will own our hiring metrics, including pass through rates by stage and by source, time to offer, offer acceptance rate, and the points in the process where candidates most often withdraw.

 - You will present those numbers in weekly hiring reviews and recommend specific changes based on what they show, rather than reporting them and waiting for direction.



Process and documentation

 - You will maintain our compressed one week interview loop as candidate volume increases, which becomes meaningfully harder as more interviewers and more open roles enter the process.

 - You will document what works clearly enough that the next person we add to this team can execute it without your involvement.

 - You will identify the points where the process slows down or produces inconsistent outcomes, and you will propose and implement fixes.



Forward planning

 - You will build candidate relationships for roles we expect to open in the next two quarters, not only for roles that are open today.




CAREER PROGRESSION

Agentio enables marketers to buy creator led ads as easily and scalably as Meta or Google ads—automating sourcing, pricing, contracting, delivery, and measurement—so work that took months now happens in minutes.

That means better outcomes for marketers and enabling creators to live off their work—finally being paid in proportion to the value they create. That shift is accelerating: Unilever's CEO has said the company will move roughly half of its ad budget into social and creators—Unilever is among the world's largest advertisers, spending around $9–10B annually. As these dollars move, they need performance-grade pipes; Agentio is how those dollars flow to creators with the speed, control, and measurement marketers expect. We enable brands like Uber, DoorDash, and Bombas to run creator campaigns with the same rigor, control, and accountability as their core performance channels.

Our AI-Native platform enables real-time content understanding at scale, simultaneous reasoning across hundreds of thousands of pieces of content, and intelligent allocation of multi-million dollar budgets. Our models apply more cross-platform performance signal than anyone else in the world, compounding with every campaign through a high-trust marketplace with accelerating network effects. The result is a flywheel: brands get the performance they've been chasing, creators get the intelligence and income they deserve, and Agentio becomes the infrastructure powering a generational shift in where media dollars flow.
